newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Asian stock markets drift as new direction sought.
newsitem.headline: Asian stock markets drift as new direction sought.

text.p: Asian markets once again found little direction on Friday, although the overall bias was weaker as investors awaited U.S. interest rate leads.
Tokyo lost nearly one percent but the move was put down to position squaring ahead of a long weekend, while Hong Kong was also defensive and gained only 0.05 percent.

Investors in the region remain wary that the U.S. Federal Reserve may opt to lift interest rates at next week's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting. Tokyo stocks closed lower as participants were prompted to square their positions ahead of the long weekend amid uncertainty about domestic politics and worries over the New York stock market before a U.S. policy-making meeting, brokers said.
The key 225-issue Nikkei average closed down 210.61 points or 0.99 percent at 21,112.24. Its key December futures shed 140 points to 21,180.
Hong Kong stocks ended with only modest gains after making a run at their year high in afternoon trade, with investors cautious ahead of next week's U.S. Federal Reserve policy meeting.
The Hang Seng index closed 5.68 points higher at 11,592.36 after reaching a session high of 11,642.54. This was just shy of its intraday year high of 11,645.35 points hit on Tuesday.
"There is a bit of caution ahead of next Tuesday's FOMC (Federal Open Market Committee) meeting," said Andrew Fernow, director of research at Vickers Ballas.
Seoul stocks closed sharply lower on across-the-board selling, pressured by an overhang of margin loans and foreign selling, brokers said.
The composite index fell 13.80 points, or 1.78 percent, to provisionally close at 759.35.
Australian stocks ended lower as the share market gyrated within a 20 point band. Heavyweight BHP swung widely after investors digested the resource giant's first quarter result.
The All Ordinaries index ended 6.3 points lower at 2240.80, but flirted in positive zones throughout the day.
Blue chips in Kuala Lumpur were lukewarm, with the Composite index ending up 2.87 points at 1,130.60.
Taiwan share prices hovered in a consolidation as the weighted index lost 36.07 points or 0.55 percent to end at 6,499.52. Turnover was an active T$51.18 billion.
Jakarta share prices closed up following active foreign buying of selected big-capitalised stocks, brokers said.
The Jakarta Composite Index rose 3.43 points, or 0.61 percent, to close at 568.99 points.
Thai stocks closed flat as market activity thinned and investors were sidelined awaiting an outcome from the censure debate against premier Banharn Silpa-archa, brokers said.
The index ended 2.48 points lower at 1,045.38 after moving in a tight 1,036.84-1,050.92 range on thin 3.47 billion baht.
Singapore shares finished lower with profit-taking seen in index-stocks after recent sharp gains. The key Straits Times Industrials Index fell 18.23 points to 2,187.86.
In Manila, the main index gained 5.19 points to 3,242.22 on selective buying.
Hong Kong gold bullion fell on professional selling from the United States and Europe and in line with weak silver prices.
Bullion ended at US$382.30/80, against New York's US$382.50/383.00 close on Thursday.
Asian crude futures were slightly lower and in late afternoon trade November Brent crude traded on Simex (The Singapore International Monetary Exchange) was down 3 cents at $21.88.
At 1030 GMT, a stronger dollar was quoted at 109.73/83 yen and 1.5160/70 marks, against 109.40/45 and 1.5135/40 at Thursday's New York close.
